design: AB1 — adaptive rho on the COLD path

changes: cap set from the hypothesis (50) instead of inherited from the R run's num_max_iters = 21
hitting the cap predeclared as INCONCLUSIVE, not a data point
primary outcome restated as cold-path cycles-to-convergence; the attractor prediction demoted to a falsifiable secondary
the control arm promoted to a deliverable in its own right
attractor prediction sharpened to the multiplicative grid, now that decrease_factor = 1.5 is confirmed
solve profile declared as a bounded claim with an identity check, since the solve count is the measurement

authorization: author, 2026-09-12: AB1 only; AB2 stays frozen. AB1 targets the cold path, the only path on which Q(x) depends on x alone and whose cost is the binding uncertainty in the project.
the_binding_condition: The cap must come from the hypothesis, not from the inherited configuration. The R run's cap of 21 is what produced a capped trajectory that was then extrapolated from — repeating it would repeat that error. BOTH arms run at an identical cap of 50 cycles.

control.status: DELIVERABLE IN ITS OWN RIGHT — this is the R trajectory finally allowed to finish. It answers what the cold path actually costs, which no existing artifact does.

treatment.penalty_update: as configured in SRP1_params.json: residual_balance_ratio 5.0, residual_balance_ratio_pf_decrease 3.0, increase_factor 1.5, decrease_factor 1.5, bounds 1e-4 to 1e4

single_varied_setting: adaptive_penalty only. Cold start, RESCALED construction, history_neutralised, identical rho, identical tolerances, identical cap, same candidate.

primary_outcome.quantity: cold-path cycles to convergence in each arm, and the local-solve count implied at 51 solves per cycle
primary_outcome.why: this is the decision-relevant number and the binding uncertainty; the attractor is secondary
primary_outcome.reporting: cycles_to_convergence, converged flag, wall clock, and solves = 51 x cycles for each arm

secondary_prediction_attractor.derivation: The pf decrease branch fires when dual_pf_mean_ratio > 3 * primal_pf_ratio, and rho is multiplied by 1/1.5 each time it fires. From rho_pf = 300 the reachable values are the multiplicative grid 300, 200, 133.33, 88.89, 59.26, ... P5.9-B settled at 131.687 = 1000/1.5^5 starting from 1000, after five consecutive decreases and a hold at cycle 6.
secondary_prediction_attractor.prediction: If the fixed point is a property of the problem and the dead band rather than of the starting value, the treatment arm settles in rho_pf in [80, 200] — most likely 133.33, the grid point adjacent to the 131.687 observed from above.
falsification: oscillation between the increase and decrease branches
secondary_prediction_attractor.caveat_recorded_in_advance: the cold-path iterates differ from the warm-path iterates, so the fixed point MAY legitimately differ. A different settling point is informative, not a failure; only oscillation or non-settling falsifies the attractor idea itself.
secondary_prediction_attractor.evidence_format: per-cycle rho_pf_before / rho_pf_after / rho_pf_action, as production already records them (shared_resources_planning.py:2507-2515), plus primal_pf_ratio and dual_pf_mean_ratio per cycle

predeclared_outcomes.adaptation_helps: treatment converges in materially fewer cycles than control with equal or better objective — the cost-versus-independence tension then largely dissolves
predeclared_outcomes.adaptation_neutral: cycle counts within one of each other
predeclared_outcomes.adaptation_harms: treatment needs more cycles, oscillates, or degrades the objective
predeclared_outcomes.INCONCLUSIVE: EITHER arm reaching cycle 50 without converging. A capped arm yields NO cold-path cost number and must not be extrapolated from. This outcome is predeclared precisely because extrapolating from a capped run is the error this design exists to avoid.

solve_profile.note: the solve count is the measurement here, so an exact predeclared count is impossible; the enforced claim is an upper bound plus an identity
solve_profile.identity_required: observed permitted solves per arm == 51 x cycles_run (+ initialization), checked after the run; a mismatch invalidates the arm
solve_profile.permitted_call_sites: the production ADMM local-solve path and the ESSO solve path

cost.per_arm_upper_bound: 2550 local solves; at P5.9-B's ~49 s/cycle this is ~41 minutes per arm at the cap
cost.expected: the treatment arm is expected to stop well before the cap; the control arm is the one that may approach it

not_permitted: changing any tolerance, criterion or rho other than the single varied setting
extrapolating a cost from a capped arm
reading the attractor result as the decision-relevant outcome
